name: Means By with a Gerund-Participial

1.definition: Presents an activity as the means by which another outcome is obtained.

examples.form: Jo reopened the file [by restoring a backup].
Jo reopened the file [after restoring a backup].
examples.note: Constructed comparison. After supplies temporal order and leaves the means relation to context.

projection.target: The restoring is interpreted as part of the method, not merely as a coincidental event in the same time period.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Saying how with by and an action word
curious.summary: By followed by an action that ends in ing says how something was done.
curious.body:
In Jo reopened the file by restoring a backup, the restoring is the method. It's how Jo got the file back. The sentence presents the activity as the means by which the outcome was reached.

Compare Jo reopened the file after restoring a backup. After gives the order of events but leaves the connection to context. By says more: the restoring is part of the method, not merely something that happened around the same time.

examples.text: Jo reopened the file [by restoring a backup].
Jo reopened the file after restoring a backup.

curious.try: Say how you got to school today, starting with by and an ing word. What would change if you used after instead?

teacher.summary: Helps explain by plus an ing phrase as the means by which something was done, and how it differs from after.
teacher.explain: A PP with by and a gerund-participial clause presents an activity as the means of obtaining another outcome: Jo reopened the file by restoring a backup. The restoring is interpreted as part of the method, not merely a coincidental event in the same time period. Compare after restoring a backup, which supplies temporal order and leaves the means relation to context. This dictionary treats the by-phrase as a specialization of the prepositional phrase and relates it to infinitival purpose adjuncts.
teacher.terms: The ing form after a preposition is traditionally called a gerund. In this dictionary it is a gerund-participial clause inside a PP.

examples.text: Jo reopened the file [by restoring a backup].

contrasts.text: Jo reopened the file by restoring a backup.
Jo reopened the file after restoring a backup.
contrasts.note: After gives temporal order; the means relation is left to context.

watch_for: A learner might read by restoring a backup as showing only when something happened, when it gives the method.
A learner might treat after restoring a backup as saying the restoring was the method, when it supplies temporal order and leaves the means to context.
teacher.activity: Students write what they did and how, using by and an ing phrase, then change by to after. Partners say whether the meaning changed and how.

child.hook: How did you get your shoes on this morning?
child.explain: You can say how you did something with by and an ing word. I opened the box by cutting the tape. The cutting is how the box got opened.

examples.text: I opened the box [by cutting the tape].
Jo reopened the file [by restoring a backup].

child.play: Say how you do something with by. I got warm by ... I made a friend by ... Finish each one with an ing word, then try after instead of by with a partner.

cite: Reynolds, Brett, ed. 2026. "Means By with a Gerund-Participial." English Constructionary. https://brettreynolds.ca/constructionary/linguist/means-by-gerund-001/ (snapshot 2026-11-19, fa37529).
